parsed.explanation: The combined regime stacks two universal exposures. Federally, an executive order fixes sex as binary at birth, eliminates the X marker, and a Feb 2025 cable directs refusal where documents cast doubt on sex, with fraud-based lifetime ineligibility considered; passports have been blocked and eight-plus governments issued travel advisories. The division adds a July 2025 law reserving all multi-occupancy restrooms, changing areas and sleeping quarters by biological sex, a private cause of action, school birth-sex rules, no state nondiscrimination or hate-crime law, and a 'worst for legislation' rating. Custody is documented: a trans woman was held 24 hours in a men's ward, and federal immigration custody records beatings and sexual abuse of trans men. Offsetting: no identity criminalisation, federal employment and hate-crime coverage, and courts enjoining several orders.

entry_documents.exposure: Sex locked to birth sex on new passports/visas, X marker ceased (Feb 2025); cable directs refusal where document discrepancy casts doubt on sex and consideration of fraud-based lifetime ineligibility; passports blocked/confiscated, travellers stranded; 8+ foreign governments issued advisories.
entry_documents.protection: Pre-2025 X-marker passports valid to expiry; fraud finding requires four elements, never automatic, limited waivers; ACLU suit pending; legal-aid FAQ on documentation strategy.
entry_documents.interaction: Border secondary screening over marker mismatch can escalate to refusal, then into immigration custody where abuse of trans detainees is documented.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Comparable state bathroom arrest (19 Mar 2025) with 24-hour hold in a men's ward; division facility law creates a private cause of action; federal corrections bureau adopted conversion-therapy-style policies (hair, hormones, drugs) and stopped counting trans prisoners; immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary and sexual abuse of trans men.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Trespass offence requires willful entry plus refusal to leave, not automatic arrest; federal 2009 hate-crime statute covers gender identity; no death penalty for identity-related conduct.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A state facility complaint can place a visitor into custody whose subsequent placement and conditions follow birth sex, with federal custody practice layered on top.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Division law (eff. 1 Jul 2025) reserves multi-occupancy restrooms, changing areas and sleeping quarters by biological sex; schools must use birth-sex facilities; federal order bars trans people from federally funded single-sex facilities; nationally 21+ units restrict facilities and 4 criminalise in some circumstances; no state gender-identity nondiscrimination law.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Three city ordinances cover gender identity in employment, housing and public accommodations; accommodations allowed where no opposite-sex multi-occupancy access; 29 units nationally have no mapped ban.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal employment protection does not reach facilities; a visitor has no state-level public-accommodation complaint route in this division.

care_services.exposure: Division bans gender-affirming care for children (eff. 1 Jul 2024) and trans sports participation (2023); proposed federal rules would bar public-insurance reimbursement for under-18 care; DOJ subpoenaed over 20 hospitals for under-19 patient records; LGBTQ youth lifeline services shut down.
care_services.protection: Adult emergency care denial is not documented; national employment discrimination protection applies since 2020.
care_services.interaction: For an adult travelling with a trans minor, the provider-facing ban forces care denial and possible state inquiry even though the parent is not the defendant.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: May 2026 counterterrorism strategy prioritises 'radically pro-transgender' groups; DOJ reward memo invokes 'radical gender ideology'; executive orders describe youth care as mutilation and direct investigation of schools; 66% of the public supports birth-sex markers on documents; division rated among worst for anti-trans legislation with four units nationally flagged 'Do Not Travel'.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Reward memo never uses ideology as a criterion; strategy states powers will not target mere disagreement; several orders blocked or enjoined; national hate-crime statute covers gender identity.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing raises both the probability of confrontation when outed and the severity of institutional responses, while chilling complaint-making.

minors_guardians.exposure: Schools must use birth-sex restrooms with only opt-out accommodation for objecting students; trans students barred from sports; youth care criminalised for providers; executive order directs criminal prosecution of teachers facilitating social transition and funding revocation for schools.
minors_guardians.protection: 'Reasonable accommodation' required for students refusing birth-sex multi-occupancy facilities; national employment protection; marriage and adoption recognition intact.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling family faces exclusion from school facilities and care, provider liability, and possible state inquiry into a guardian accompanying a socially transitioned child.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No state hate-crime statute and only 23 units cover gender identity in bias statutes; travel guidance advises checking recent violence reports; documented restroom arrest with men's-ward holding; no state nondiscrimination law.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Federal 2009 hate-crime statute covers gender identity; three city ordinances; no documented pattern of trans killings in the dossier; same-sex conduct legal since 1977.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police responding to a facility complaint under the division law can initiate the arrest-to-birth-sex-custody chain.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Whether the division facility law has been challenged or enforced is not sourced; the 'worst legislation' rating's specific bills are unverifiable; corrections stopped reporting trans prisoner counts; no state public-accommodation claim exists; which measures are in force on a given travel date is uncertain.
remedies_unknowns.protection: ACLU suit pending and multiple executive orders enjoined; legal-aid FAQ maintained; national employment claims available through the labour agency and courts; federal hate-crime statute.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Federal remedies operate on documents and employment, not on facility exclusion or custody placement, so the operative exposures remain unremedied.

anchor_checks.comparison: Saruth combines routine post-inspection detention, assaults in cells, withheld care and courts deferring to police. This jurisdiction lacks routine custodial abuse for ordinary visitors, has functioning federal courts that have enjoined orders, and no capital dimension, so it is materially safer; but documented birth-sex ward holding and immigration-custody abuse keep it from the 0.60+ range.

Vesskar's routine checkpoint exposure, detentions, humiliation, denial of care, narrow claims and scarce legal aid closely parallels the border-mismatch and facility regime here. This dossier is somewhat worse on codification (a statewide facility statute with a private cause of action, an arrest precedent, no state recourse) and worse on custody placement, so it sits slightly below.

Kestrel Isles offers discretionary secondary screening, refused admission and slow appeals with no criminal escalation. The border exposure here is comparable, but the division adds universal facility exclusion, birth-sex custody placement with reported harm, and a youth-care ban affecting travelling families, pushing the rating well below this anchor.

Meridia trains border staff, accepts matching markers, guarantees written reasons, counsel and compensation for unlawful holding. Here markers cannot be aligned, foreign governments warn their citizens, facilities are statutorily excluded, and custody follows birth sex. Far below this anchor: the protections that would be needed simply do not operate.

parsed.synthesis: Two universal-exposure regimes compound. The federal document regime guarantees a mismatch for any visibly trans traveller, and the Feb 2025 cable converts that mismatch into a refusal risk with a fraud-escalation pathway; several governments now advise against travel. In-division, the July 2025 facilities statute excludes the visitor from every multi-occupancy restroom, changing area and sleeping quarter, backed by a private cause of action and a documented arrest precedent in a comparable unit, with custody then following birth sex (24-hour men's-ward hold). No state nondiscrimination or hate-crime law fills the gap, and the division is rated among the worst for anti-trans legislation. Mitigation is real but partial: federal employment and hate-crime coverage, city ordinances, and courts that have enjoined several orders — none of which reach facilities, border documents, or custody placement. For an adult with a trans minor, the youth-care and school bans add provider liability and exclusion. No criminalisation of identity and no execution risk keep this above the 0.35 tier; unremedied tier-1 exposures keep it below 0.60.
